Even streets in many central high-rise districts can briefly turn into rivers, with rats and cockroaches racing out of sewers and taking temporary refuge on trees and buildings as the subterranean world is flushed out.

But every city has a breaking point, and this year rain fell so fast and so hard that whole neighbourhoods of the Thai capital have been transformed, not into rivers, but stagnant lakes. In parts of the city, roughly 300mm of rain – the equivalent of half a year of average rainfall in London – fell in about two days.

events.title: What would Francis of Assisi make of his fame today?
events.summary: The Catholic saint renounced wealth and fame to become a mendicant friar. Yet throughout history, his teachings and life have inspired popes, Dante and even Mussolini.

events.title: European cities seek ways of boosting affordable housing
events.summary: In many major urban centers of Europe, the housing shortage has become an explosive social issue. DW looks into various models that have been put in place across the continent.

events.title: Germany news: Are Germans giving up their beloved meat and sausages?
events.summary: Germans used to be all about sausages and meat. While those do remain popular, things seem to be slowly changing. There also are new insights into the economic side of East Germany's espionage DW has more.

events.title: Backlash over data centers tests Europe's AI ambitions
events.summary: Massive data centers needed to run AI are triggering protests across Europe. Their operators counter that they boost digital sovereignty and energy independence.

events.title: Russia expected to intensify hybrid war on Europe
events.summary: Drone explosions, airspace violations, arson attacks: Poland, Romania, and Moldova are now regularly targeted in Russian attacks against Ukraine. More governments are calling these attacks deliberate acts of aggression.

events.title: DW shows solidarity with Georgians' commitment to democracy
events.summary: Cultural and media professionals in Georgia remain under threat. A DW panel brings together insiders who share their hopes and fears.

events.title: Bundesliga, other top European leagues call for major FIFA reforms
events.summary: The Bundesliga and three other leading European football leagues have said major reforms to world-governing body FIFA are "essential." However, they stopped short of calling for the resignation of boss Gianni Infantino.

events.title: Jürgen Klopp starts Germany job with shaky Netherlands draw
events.summary: A late Netherlands goal denied Jürgen Klopp a win in his first match as Germany coach. The former Liverpool and Borussia Dortmund boss has big ambitions, but the game showed he's going to need more time to achieve them.

events.title: Three-way battle for power in world chess: Who will be elected FIDE president in Samarkand?
events.summary: The era of Russian presidents is coming to an end at the World Chess Federation (FIDE). Two Germans and one Kazakh are up for election. Among the issues at play are money, Kremlin influence, and unanswered questions.

events.title: After several difficult years, economists now expect German economy to grow
events.summary: Germany's economy is growing again, but recovery remains on shaky ground. High government spending is keeping the economy afloat, while energy prices, a shortage of skilled workers and debt continue to weigh on it.

events.title: Political psychology: Why extremist parties are thriving and what democratic politicians can do against it
events.summary: Far-right and far-left parties are celebrating success after success, leaving moderate politicians in the dust and worrying many Germans. Political psychology helps us understand what's behind growing polarization.

events.title: Could flattering AI make humanity turn on itself?
events.summary: A study shows chatbots mirror users' politics, part of a broader tendency known as AI sycophancy. Researchers fear this could deepen polarization.

events.title: Germany news: Berlin officially withdraws Olympics bid
events.summary: Berlin's decision to withdraw its Olympic bid means that only Munich and the western Rhine/Ruhr region are left in the running as potential Olympic hosts. DW has more.

events.title: Could a Left Party government in Berlin expropriate large real estate companies?
events.summary: The socialist Left Party won the Berlin election partly on the promise to implement the city's 2021 expropriation referendum as a way to solve the city's rent crisis. But can it really happen?

events.title: China's 13-year-old swimming star raises questions on child athletes
events.summary: Three gold medals and three Asian Games records have catapulted China's Yu Zidi, 13, into the sporting spotlight. She is far from the first teen prodigy, but should teens be competing at elite level?

events.title: Germany's oldest party, the center-left SPD, is in a difficult position following its success in the Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania state election
events.summary: Chancellor Friedrich Merz (CDU) has vowed to press ahead with controversial reforms, but resistance is mounting within his coalition partner, the SPD. How much dissent can a governing coalition tolerate?

events.title: Munich and Cologne-Rhine-Ruhr – Germany's two remaining Olympic candidates
events.summary: Munich or the Cologne-Rhine-Ruhr region? Germany aims to host the Olympic Games again. Just two candidates are left after Berlin pulled out at the last minute.

events.title: El Nino explained: How the weather pattern affects hurricanes and tropical storms
events.summary: From drought to major floods and extreme heat, El Nino will have a huge impact on the world's weather. In the Atlantic, it could mean a season without hurricanes.

events.title: China's new travel rules unsettle tech giants and talent
events.summary: Beijing is locking the gates to stop expertise and capital in strategic industries from fleeing. The country accused of industrial-scale intellectual property theft now fears the West will take its own.

events.title: Germany news: Call to scrap once-a-day gas price rises
events.summary: The ADAC motoring association says a once-a-day rule on gas price changes has failed to help drivers' wallets. Entry-level jobs are becoming scarcer, making things hard for those entering the job market. DW has more.

events.title: Young Berliners vote overwhelmingly for socialist Left  Party
events.summary: Berlin's young voters overwhelmingly supported the victorious socialist Left Party. Are the young more radical? Or are the election results just a reflection of current German politics?

events.title: Living in the shadow of LA's hidden oil wells
events.summary: Many lifelong residents of Los Angeles have health impacts from growing up close to oil extraction. Now, the city is trying to close down the worst offenders, but it's an enormous task.

events.title: Could we see MMA at the Olympics?
events.summary: Mixed martial arts has made its debut at the Asian Games this week. It takes the sport closer to the Olympics, but there are doubts about the next step — and the influence of the popular and lucrative UFC.

events.title: Male infertility is 'grossly underreported'
events.summary: It's not all on women anymore — doctors do test men for sperm count and motility. But still too few men get checked, possibly due to a misconception that a healthy sex life means healthy sperm. Spoiler: It doesn't.

events.title: Will Germany have enough gas this winter amid energy supply crunch?
events.summary: Germany's gas storage sites are far less full than in recent years. Officials say supplies are secure, but analysts warn that a cold winter or import disruptions could push prices higher. So how secure is the supply?

events.title: Germany news: VW to step up cost-cutting program
events.summary: Volkswagen's chief says the carmaker will accelerate its streamlining measures as workers protest. The Israeli ambassador says the Left Party win in Berlin polls poses a risk to the city's Jewish community. DW has more.

events.title: How will Germany's Merz respond after crushing state election results and losses to the far right?
events.summary: Germany's far-right AfD and the socialist Left Party gained ground in recent state elections, while the centrist parties lost support. The biggest loser is Chancellor Friedrich Merz.

events.title: Princess Diana's brother makes explosive claims about royals in new memoir
events.summary: Here are some of the key revelations from Charles Earl Spencer's highly anticipated memoir "Swan Song: Diana, My Sister." It has already provoked Buckingham Palace to react.

events.title: Germany news: Trial starts of ex-Transport Minister Scheuer
events.summary: Former Transport Minister Andreas Scheuer is being tried for perjury related to a failed car toll scheme. And cherry farmers have brought in a bumper harvest.

events.title: Germany's car crisis: Can the 35-hour workweek survive?
events.summary: German carmakers want employees to work 40 hours instead of the current 35 without extra pay, arguing it would improve competitiveness. Unions strongly oppose the proposal and view it as an attack on workers' rights.

events.title: Germany faces energy tax losses as EV sales rise
events.summary: The rapid shift to electric vehicles in Germany is cutting fuel tax revenue for the government. As EV sales surge, policymakers face growing pressure to find new ways to fund roads and transportation infrastructure.

events.title: Summer of 2026 broke records in Europe, and caused deaths
events.summary: The summer of 2026 was not only the hottest on record in Europe, it also saw a record number of people die. More than 16,000 are thought to have died because of the heat in Germany alone.

events.title: Oktoberfest 2026: Everything you need to know
events.summary: This year, AI will be used to manage overcrowded situations. Find all the numbers surrounding the fest — including the price of water!

events.title: Rebels, workers, radicals: The making of 'Red Berlin'
events.summary: Bloody May, student sit-ins and the squatter movement: Berlin has long been a hotbed for working-class organizing and radical left-wing politics.

events.title: Women's football in Germany booming, but still much to do
events.summary: Women's football is growing rapidly, particularly in Germany. Nevertheless, equal pay and investment remain major talking points.

events.title: Strait of Hormuz attacks spill oil into Persian Gulf
events.summary: As war disrupts one of the world's busiest shipping lanes, satellite images reveal that oil is spreading toward protected coral reefs and mangrove forests.

events.title: Dual citizenship means Germany now in competition for talent
events.summary: Coach Jürgen Klopp has named several players to his first Germany squad who are eligible to play for other countries. Some still aren't committed to playing for thje national team long-term.

events.title: Beethoven and Andy Warhol: Rebel icons on show in Bonn
events.summary: The new exhibition "Beethoven by Warhol" at the Beethoven House in Bonn presents the pop artist's late masterpiece: a picture of Ludwig van Beethoven. The exhibition shares the story of the work with the public.

events.title: VAR's mission creep a problem for football
events.summary: After a decade of use, questions around VAR in football are louder than ever. Has the technology strayed too far from its remit?

events.title: Alexander Ovechkin backs Putin party in campaign video
events.summary: Ice hockey legend Alexander Ovechkin has lent Vladimir Putin's party a helping hand in its parliamentary election campaign. That's in keeping with a pattern of support by an athlete who claims not to be political.

events.title: Klopp wants Germany's football team to 'reclaim the flag'
events.summary: Jürgen Klopp, Germany's new head coach, says he wants his team to reclaim pride in being German after recent political developments.

events.title: Jews once lived lived here: When houses tell stories
events.summary: Time and again, residents tracing the history of their homes discover the lives of Jewish predecessors who fled or were deported amid stories of suffering and loss.

events.title: Jürgen Klopp's first Germany squad includes 44 players
events.summary: Germany's new head coach Jürgen Klopp has named a huge squad for his first four games, splitting them into two groups. A host of new faces is included.

events.title: Saint, sinner or feminist icon: How Mary Magdalene's image evolved through time
events.summary: From "Apostle of the Apostles" to prostitute, Mary Magdalene has been assigned a wide variety of roles, as a new exhibition shows.

events.title: How climate change worsened Nepal's deadly mountain collapse
events.summary: A glacier and rock collapse in Nepal killed nearly 1,400 people and left thousands missing. Scientists say decades of warming helped set the disaster in motion.

events.title: After Neuer: Who will be Germany's new No. 1 goalkeeper?
events.summary: Following Manuel Neuer's retirement, there are many candidates to succeed him, but which goalkeeper will Jürgen Klopp choose? What factors will play a role? And will Neuer's future have an indirect influence?

events.title: Global Gender Gap Report: Women's hard-won gains 'fragile'
events.summary: Two decades of progress toward gender parity is at risk as women's political representation declines, according to a new World Economic Forum report. At the current pace, the remaining gap could take 120 years to close.

events.title: German drama 'Blindspot Berlin' revisits 2016 Christmas market attack
events.summary: A decade after the terrorist attack on a Berlin Christmas market, a new German miniseries looks into the institutional failures that allowed the deadly truck rampage to happen.

events.title: How extreme heat is hitting wallets
events.summary: Heat waves, wildfires and floods have cascading economic impacts, causing incomes to decline and the price of basic goods to rise. The trend will escalate as temperatures continue to increase.

events.title: Spanish scientists find first evidence of Diplodocus dinosaur in Europe
events.summary: Paleontologists in Spain say they have found the first evidence of the long-necked Diplodocus genus of dinosaur outside of North America. They found bones at the rich La Tejeria fossil site in Teruel in eastern Spain.

events.title: Why the era of cheap government debt is over
events.summary: US debt has topped $40 trillion. How risky is the country's growing debt burden. And will investors keep funding Washington's deficits?

events.title: Why AI researchers warn humanity could face extinction
events.summary: Could artificial intelligence pose an existential threat to humanity? Some leading researchers are warning against an unregulated race toward AI superintelligence.

events.title: Iran and US: Two countries and the pistachio between them
events.summary: The pistachios sold across the United States have a surprising history: California's trees trace their roots to Iran. Now, both regions face the same threat — their farmland is sinking as groundwater disappears.

events.title: Women's Basketball World Cup: Can Germany harness a boom?
events.summary: Germany thrilled fans at the Women's Basketball World Cup. But even if this sparked a boom in the women's game, the infrastructure simply isn't ready for it.

events.title: Africa's richest man Dangote's IPO out of reach in Nigeria
events.summary: Dangote seeks $1.6 billion from investors to finance a $14.3 billion expansion and thus double the oil refinery's capacity. The offer could give millions of Nigerians a stake in the company. But who can truly afford it?

events.title: The Crusades: How a medieval holy war still shapes politics
events.summary: In 1095, the Catholic Church launched the Crusades: wars that left millions dead and whose legacy still shapes political and ideological conflicts.

events.title: Can Iran replace sea trade with land routes?
events.summary: Iran is shifting trade toward northern ports and land routes as its southern shipping faces a US blockade. Analysts say the corridors can keep essential goods moving, but cannot replace maritime trade.

events.title: Why are European banks moving gold out of United States?
events.summary: The Netherlands and France have moved their gold out of US vaults. Part of the reason is fears about the reliability of the US, but equally important is the need to keep gold closer to home in the event of a crisis.

events.title: Corals as climate archive: Are El Nino events intensifying?
events.summary: Records show that El Nino events have been frequent and often extreme over the past few decades. Is this normal? Or is it the result of climate change? Corals can give us a clear indication.

events.title: India looks to steer BRICS away from anti-Western turn
events.summary: The BRICS summit 2026 takes place in Delhi this weekend. Unlike last year, Putin and Xi are expected to attend. Can India keep the expanded bloc united?

events.title: The 'end of an era' as Goethe-Institut in Russia closes
events.summary: The Goethe-Institut was one of the last German institutions still operating in Russia. However, following Moscow's decision to close its offices, all employees will have to stop working by September 13.

events.title: How Celine Dion became a pop culture icon across generations
events.summary: As the global star kicks off her anticipated Paris residency, here's how Celine Dion managed to gain younger followers while keeping her loyal older fans.

events.title: How Belarusians still find hope in a silenced country
events.summary: The documentary "Letters from the Silenced Country" depicts the ongoing repression under the authoritarian regime. Director Andrei Kutsila talked to DW ahead of the film's Venice premiere.

events.title: Why we're still looking for dark matter
events.summary: When physicists said they may have spotted evidence of dark matter almost 100 years after it was proposed as a theory, the internet lit up. Here's why we're searching for the thing that holds everything else together.

events.title: Conspiracy theories can provide answers but not peace
events.summary: Twenty-five years after 9/11, conspiracy theories about the terrorist attacks persist. But even as an attempt to make sense of a tragedy, psychologists say the benefit in conspiracy ideation or belief is short-lived.

events.title: The billion-euro trade driving Europe's eels to extinction
events.summary: Traffickers are making big bucks smuggling millions of critically endangered eels across continents, using suitcases on planes and legal loopholes to deliver them to dinnerplates. Where are the smuggling hotspots?

events.title: The Bayeux Tapestry in London: What's behind the hype?
events.summary: The exhibition of the Bayeux Tapestry at the British Museum is eagerly anticipated across the UK, as the medieval masterpiece is considered by many to be a symbol of the country's identity.

events.title: PISA 2025 results: Reading and math scores plummet worldwide
events.summary: The PISA 2025 results reveal record-low student performance, with digital distractions and AI use raising concerns. Germany is faring worse than ever.

events.title: Werner Herzog: Germany's wild man of cinema is back
events.summary: As his latest movie, "Bucking Fastard," premiered at the Venice Film Festival, DW talked to the boundary-breaking director.

events.title: Croatia: Toxic waste protest draws tens of thousands
events.summary: The Zagreb demonstrators demanded that the government come up with a plan to clear illegal toxic waste in 20 days. Prime Minister Plenkovic has promised to tackle the issue.

events.title: Germany: From emigration to immigration destination
events.summary: Migration is a sensitive topic in Germany, with public debate dominated by the fear of uncontrolled immigration. But over two centuries, millions of Germans emigrated in search of a better life.

events.title: Iran says no military solution to war as peace talks with US stall
events.summary: Iran's diplomat said on Sunday there was no military solution to the US war against Iran as peace talks appeared stalled. Washington has scaled back attacks in favour of economic pressure, while Iran's attempted Hormuz blockade remains contentious. A UK maritime agency reported another tanker hit by an unidentified projectile.

events.title: A Profile of Brazil's Potential President
events.summary: France 24's Gavin Lee speaks to Brazil analyst Henrique Tavares Furtado about how Flavio Bolsonaro is pledging to reshape the country, and asks: who is the man behind the political persona?

events.title: Brazil heads to the polls for high-stakes election between Lula and Flavio Bolsonaro
events.summary: Brazilians began casting their votes on Sunday in a closely watch presidential election pitting incumbent President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva against right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, son of former president Jair Bolsonaro. Nearly 160 million voters will also pick lawmakers, senators and governors in an election that will determine whether Latin America's biggest nation follows a regional swing to the right championed by US President Donald Trump. France24 International affairs commentator Douglas Herbert shares further insights.

events.title: Evenepoel snatches photo-finish win to clinch European road cycling crown
events.summary: Belgium's Olympic road racing champion Remco Evenepoel took the European championship title on Sunday after outsprinting Italy's Giulio Ciccone in a tight photo finish, just weeks after narrowly missing out on the world championship crown.

events.title: Woman at centre of Cornell gang rape lawsuit targeted with threats, lawyer says
events.summary: The woman who alleged that she was drugged and raped by seven male students at a Cornell University fraternity house has been the target of threats, her lawyer told CNN on Sunday. Cornell's president earlier voiced support for an external review of the Ivy League institution facing widespread outcry over its handling of the case.

events.title: German Chancellor in Kyiv: "Ukraine will need our support"
events.summary: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz visited Ukraine on Sunday to show solidarity after Russian attacks on Kyiv infrastructure, including three bridges. Last month, Germany’s foreign minister called for de-escalation during talks with his Russian counterpart at the UN, drawing criticism from Sergei Lavrov, who urged Berlin to stop arming Ukraine. On Saturday, Moscow called on foreign nationals and diplomats to leave Ukraine. Shirli Sitbon reports.

events.title: Why I quit the movement shaping AI
events.summary: Artificial intelligence insiders are quitting their jobs, saying the technology could mean the end of humanity. Pope Leo in France warned of a “paradise of machines”. And the New York Times reported this week that one of AI firm Anthropic’s co-founders spent months lobbying religious thinkers on the possibility that AI could be conscious.

events.title: The week in pictures: Disaster averted on Flydubai flight, French school protests and Bangkok floods
events.summary: From French highschoolers protesting to demand better learning conditions to a Flydubai flight diverted to Saudi Arabia after a flightcrew member's onboard attack and flooded streets in Bangkok, FRANCE 24 looks back at the week's most striking pictures.

events.title: Brazil: Lula and Bolsonaro tied in polls
events.summary: Brazilians began casting their votes on Sunday in a closely watch presidential election pitting incumbent President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva against right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, son of former president Jair Bolsonaro. Mara Nogueira, Senior Lecturer in Urban Geography at Birbeck, University of London, says the tight race reflects the consolidation of two political camps, with many Brazilians voting not out of support for a candidate, but to keep the other out of power. She points to the cost of living, religion and social media echo chambers as key factors shaping the vote, alongside a major banking scandal that has so far had limited impact on Flavio Bolsonaro’s campaign.

events.title: Lula de Silva: 80-year-old incumbent Brazilian president seeks 4th term
events.summary: Brazilians began casting their votes on Sunday in a closely watch presidential election pitting incumbent President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva against right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, son of former president Jair Bolsonaro. Nearly 160 million voters will also pick lawmakers, senators and governors in an election that will determine whether Latin America's biggest nation follows a regional swing to the right championed by US President Donald Trump. France 24 correspondent Jan Onoszko tells us the latest from Rio de Janeiro.

events.title: Yemen's government declares counter-offensive as Houthis cut vital route to besieged city
events.summary: The ​leader of ​Yemen's Saudi-backed government announced the beginning of a ​major ‌military ⁠operation against the Iran-backed Houthis ‌on Sunday aimed at ⁠recapturing territory under their control. The announcement came as Houthi forces cut off a vital supply route to the besieged government-held city of Taiz, according to several security sources.

events.title: Hundreds of schools to shut Monday as France braces for more student protests
events.summary: France's education minister said lessons would be "totally or partly suspended" at up to 500 high schools on Monday after several days of sometimes violent protests against teacher shortages, dilapidated school buildings and overcrowding in classrooms. The minister said 24 schools had been "burned or ransacked" since the start of the protest movement.

events.title: Rwandan genocide suspect 'hunter' Dafroza Gauthier dies at 72
events.summary: For nearly 30 years, Dafroza Gauthier, along with her husband Alain, tracked down Rwandan refugees in France suspected of having participated in the Tutsi genocide. She died in Reims on Saturday after dedicating her life to bringing to justice those allegedly responsible for the 1994 massacre of more than 800,000 people.

events.title: West Bank: Palestinians ‘harassed’ by settlers’ increasing use of drones
events.summary: Palestinians and activists report an increased use of drones in the occupied West Bank, particularly by the army and settlers, to whom the government supplies the drones directly. The drones are used to intimidate, monitor, demolish and make daily life unbearable.

events.title: Lula and Bolsonaro face off in Brazil presidential race
events.summary: Twelve candidates are on the ballot, but the presidential race is centred on two rivals: President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and Flavio Bolsonaro. Lula is seeking a fourth and final term, warning that Brazil’s sovereignty is at stake amid pressure from Donald Trump. Bolsonaro, meanwhile, has highlighted his ties to the White House, saying Brazil needs better deals with the US, including over its rare mineral resources. Nick Rushworth has more on the controversial senator. Dr Andrea Aruska de Souza Santos, Director of King's College Brazil Institute in London, shares further insights.

events.title: Cornell president breaks silence over alleged campus rape
events.summary: Cornell University remains at the centre of controversy over an alleged gang rape at a fraternity on campus, with the university president now breaking his silence. In an eight-minute video statement released Saturday night, Michael Kotlikoff called the allegations, made by a woman known as Jane Doe, deeply disturbing and said the university must do better. Shirli Sitbon has this report.

events.title: Polls close in Brazil's high-stakes election pitting Lula against Flavio Bolsonaro
events.summary: Brazilians voted Sunday in a high-stakes presidential election pitting incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva against far-right challenger Flavio Bolsonaro, following a campaign dominated by corruption scandals, economic anxiety and accusations of US meddling. The knife-edge election comes at a moment when the region is shifting to the right in line with the Trump administration.

events.title: Israel prepares to mark October 7
events.summary: An Israeli strike on a civilian vehicle in Gaza on Sunday killed one Palestinian and wounded at least 11 others. Israel’s military said it was targeting a Hamas militant. Palestinians have reported a surge in Israeli fire and airstrikes across Gaza over the past month, with more than 75,000 people killed and much of the enclave destroyed. Meanwhile, Israelis held their weekly protest in Tel Aviv’s Hostages Square, the last before Wednesday marks three years since the October 7 attack. Protesters said they wanted to commemorate the victims and demand an independent state inquiry into the events and decisions that led to the attack. The Hamas-led assault killed around 1,200 people in Israel and saw more than 250 others taken hostage, according to Israeli authorities. Rachael Goldberg Polin, an American-Israeli activist and mother of slain hostage Hersh Goldberg-Polin, speaks to France 24.

events.title: Ethiopian federal forces control Tigray capital as regional rivals meet in Egypt
events.summary: Troops loyal to Ethiopia's federal government were patrolling the streets of Mekelle on Sunday, a day after the Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF) withdrew its forces from the northern city. The government advance came as Ethiopia's regional rivals including Eritrea and Sudan met in the Egyptian coastal city of El-Alamein, calling for regional disputes to be settled through "peaceful means".

events.title: Russian strike hits Kyiv amid Chancellor Merz visit
events.summary: Moscow has once again bombed one of Kyiv’s bridges, despite the presence of German Chancellor Friedrich Merz in the Ukrainian capital. The visit was unplanned, but Merz says it was intended to show Germany’s support for Ukraine. France 24 correspondent Gulliver Cragg, reporting from Kyiv, says traffic has resumed on the bridge, though slowly. Video shows a large hole in the roadway. Experts say the bridges are extremely solid and difficult to destroy, even with ballistic missiles.

events.title: Brazil: A portrait of Flavio Bolsonaro
events.summary: Brazilians are voting for governors and lawmakers, but the biggest stakes are in the presidential race. Twelve candidates are on the ballot, but the contest is seen as a toss-up between President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and Flavio Bolsonaro. Lula is seeking a fourth and final term, warning that Brazil’s sovereignty is at stake amid pressure from Donald Trump. Bolsonaro, meanwhile, has highlighted his ties to the White House, saying Brazil needs better deals with the US, including over its rare mineral resources. Nick Rushworth has more on the controversial senator.

events.title: Who are the mystery pilots who successfully landed endangered Flydubai flight 1073?
events.summary: A passenger on Flydubai flight 1073 has described the actions of on-duty crew members who rushed into the cockpit to stabilise and land the plane after the co-pilot attacked the captain with a crash axe. The flight carrying 182 people en route to Israel Wednesday was able to make an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia after a descent so extreme that part of its rudder was torn away.

events.title: Le Pen stands by top ally Bardella as anti-Semitism claims hit star of French far right
events.summary: French far-right presidential candidate Marine Le Pen has reiterated her "complete confidence" in National Rally (RN) leader Jordan Bardella, accused by investigative news outlet Mediapart of making anti-Semitic comments in 2013. But some analysts say the frontrunner in the Élysée Palace race may seek to distance herself from her protégé should the controversy end up damaging her campaign.

events.title: Tsar Samuel laid to rest in Sofia
events.summary: In Bulgaria, the remains of medieval ruler Tsar Samuel have been laid to rest in the capital Sofia, after being flown back from the border with Greece by Bulgarian fighter jets. Their return follows decades of negotiations with Athens, in exchange for the return of religious artefacts. Nicholas Rushworth has more.

events.title: 'We manage together': Meet the psychologist helping Ukraine's veterans live again
events.summary: "Often they feel superfluous, as if they don't fit in," says psychologist Yevheniia Zhuravel.

events.title: Ireland's football media call ends in chaos
events.summary: Republic of Ireland's Nations League press conference descended into chaos after Israeli journalists started asking questions about the flydubai attack and alleged racial abuse of players.

events.title: Thousands of Imran Khan supporters march towards Pakistan's barricaded capital
events.summary: Supporters of Imran Khan, Pakistan's former prime minister, have started a march towards the capital Islamabad to demand his release from prison.

events.title: Flydubai co-pilot: Australian links probed after 'axe attack' on captain
events.summary: Australian authorities are investigating a flydubai co-pilot's "links to Australia"  after he attacked the captain ​on a Tel Aviv-bound flight.

events.title: Witness sought after death of man pinned down by security guards
events.summary: Police investigating the death of a Congolese man after he was pinned down by security guards in Dublin city centre want to speak to a woman knocked to the ground during the incident.

events.title: Tens of thousands protest against Spain's housing crisis
events.summary: Tens of thousands of people have taken to the streets of Spanish cities in protest at the country's housing crisis in the wake of the forcible eviction of 87-year-old Maricarmen Abascal.

events.title: Opposition fighters withdraw from capital of Ethiopia's northern Tigray region
events.summary: Government-allied fighters entered Mekelle, the capital of Ethiopia's northern Tigray region, a witness said, after the rebel Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF) announced its withdrawal.

events.title: At least 17 people killed in Kenya road crash
events.summary: At least 17 people were killed in a road crash involving several vehicles on the highway from the Kenyan coastal city of Mombasa to the capital, Nairobi.

events.title: North Korea fires ballistic missile after Seoul demands apology
events.summary: North Korea's Kim Yo Jong, the powerful sister of leader Kim ​Jong Un, has said that her country tested an intermediate-range strategic missile.

events.title: Ten injured as car hits crowd in Australia in 'horrible incident'
events.summary: Ten people have been injured, including several children, after a car drove into a crowd gathered to cheer on a rugby team on Saturday, Australian officials have said.

events.title: An immigrant deported by the US and held in an African prison for more than a year has been released
events.summary: A Laos citizen deported by the United States to Eswatini in Africa under the Trump administration’s immigration crackdown has been released after spending more than a year in a maximum security prison

events.title: Dozens detained at Kremlin-friendly Communist Party's Moscow rally, party says
events.summary: Police detained about 60 people, mostly young, as the rally was ending.

events.title: US Marine arrested for alleged killing of a woman on Okinawa, triggers outrage from Japan
events.summary: Japanese police say they have arrested a U.S. Marine for the alleged robbery and killing of a woman on Okinawa

events.title: The Latest: Brazilians vote in presidential election dominated by Lula and Bolsonaro
events.summary: Brazilians are voting in a pivotal presidential election featuring incumbent Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Sen. Flávio Bolsonaro

events.title: Opposition fighters in northern Ethiopia's Tigray withdraw from regional capital
events.summary: Government-allied fighters have entered Mekelle, the capital of Ethiopia’s Tigray region, after the Tigray People’s Liberation Front announced its withdrawal

events.title: 2 people killed in Norway after shooter opens fire on hunting party
events.summary: Two people were killed and another seriously injured when a shooter opened fire on a hunting party in southern Norway

events.title: Pro-Ukraine governing coalition wins 35% in Latvian election

events.summary: Demonstrators across France are clashing with police as protests continue over what some students claims are teacher shortages and poor classroom conditions. NBC News’ Richard Engel reports.

events.title: With more deaths than births in Ukraine, having babies becomes an act of national pride
events.summary: With deaths outnumbering births in Ukraine by more than 3 to 1, having babies in a war-torn country becomes an act of national pride, and even survival. NBC News' Richard Engel reports from an underground bomb shelter turned delivery room.

events.title: Co-pilot attacker had been banned from flying over his radical views
events.summary: The Wall Street Journal reports the co-pilot who tried to fly a plane bound for Israel into the ground had been banned from flying by his home country, Oman, over his radical views. Plus, an Israeli official told NBC News investigators discovered the co-pilot had posted on social media that he wanted to kill Jews. NBC News’ Matt Bradley reports.

events.title: New video of hero passengers from plane attack
events.summary: New video showed the heroic Israeli passengers who subdued a co-pilot who tried to bring down their FlyDubai flight. President Trump said the co-pilot has links to Iran. NBC News’ Matt Bradley reports.

events.title: How an American teacher’s $5,000 donation helped turn a Chinese desert into a lush forest
events.summary: Ronald Sakolsky couldn’t believe his eyes when he visited China’s Mu Us Desert for the first time in 26 years. “Seeing it with my own eyes, that was the biggest surprise,” he said.

events.title: Anger grows across Spain after elderly woman is evicted from her home of 70 years
events.summary: An 87-year-old Spanish woman was forcibly evicted Wednesday from the Madrid apartment she had lived in for more than 70 years, in a case that highlights a growing housing crisis in the country.

events.title: U.S. Air Force removes all bombers from British air base targeted in a suspected terrorist plot
events.summary: The bombers at RAF Fairford “have been re-deployed to their home stations in the United States,” a Pentagon official told NBC News.

events.title: U.S. Marine arrested on suspicion of killing Japanese woman in Okinawa
events.summary: Japan’s Defense Ministry said it was “deeply outraged by the extremely brutal and heinous crime committed by a U.S. Marine.”

events.title: Flydubai pilot attacked captain with cockpit’s crash ax in attempted terrorist act, UAE official says
events.summary: TEL AVIV — A Flydubai pilot attacked his flight captain using a crash ax and tried to take control of the aircraft’s controls in an attempted terrorist attack, an official with the United Arab Emirates said Saturday.

events.title: Two Iranian nationals charged over alleged terrorism plot targeting Jewish community in England
events.summary: British police said Friday that they had charged two Iranian nationals accused of plotting a terrorist attack against the Jewish community in Manchester on the eve of Yom Kippur, the holiest day in the Jewish calendar.

events.title: Screaming, panicking, blood: Passengers detail horrifying Israel-bound flight
events.summary: It was too early to say why a pilot stabbed another on the flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv, according to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

events.title: What we know about the cockpit stabbing on Israel-bound flight
events.summary: What we know about the potential midair disaster aboard the Flydubai flight when a pilot attacked his colleague causing the plane to plunge thousands of feet.

events.title: Britain believes Iran was involved in incident near air base used by U.S., prime minister says
events.summary: Five men were arrested on suspicion of terrorist offenses in the incident outside RAF Fairford. Iran had denied any involvement.

events.title: What we know about the pilot hailed as a hero for averting crash of Israel-bound plane
events.summary: He is being hailed around the world as a hero for helping stop a passenger plane bound for Israel from plunging into the ground, despite his own severe injuries.

events.title: Pilot stabbed his co-pilot in apparent attempt to crash Israel-bound plane, Netanyahu says
events.summary: On-duty crewmembers were able to divert and land the aircraft safely at Tabuk Airport, the airline said.

events.title: British police find no explosives in vehicles of men detained near base used by U.S.
events.summary: Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the incident near RAF Fairford, which facilitates strikes on Iran, “clearly involves the hands of a foreign actor,” an allegation British officials haven’t confirmed.

events.title: Settlers clash with Israeli forces to block Palestinian family’s return home
events.summary: It is the second time the Tubassi family has suffered at the hands of Jewish settlers in just over a month. On Aug. 28, masked settlers attacked and injured them and an NBC News crew that was interviewing them.

events.title: A search for their loved ones’ remains, three months after Venezuela earthquakes
events.summary: Sleeping in tents in front of collapsed buildings and removing rubble with bare hands, family members and volunteers search the ruins with at least 1,500 people missing.

events.title: Terrorism suspects arrested near British air base used by U.S. are released on bail
events.summary: The five British nationals were detained after a massive security operation near a base the U.S. uses to facilitate strikes on Iran.

events.title: Five men arrested on terror charge near British base used by U.S.
events.summary: The incident triggered a massive response, with homes evacuated and bomb disposal teams searching three vans close to the base.
